newsitem.title: USA: Unisource to sell unit to Bunzl for $88 million.
newsitem.headline: Unisource to sell unit to Bunzl for $88 million.

text.p: Unisource Worldwide Inc., a paper products and supply systems distributor, said Friday it has agreed to sell its grocery supply systems unit and related U.S. operations to British company Bunzl Plc for about $88 million in cash.

Although Unisource is pleased with the growth of its U.S. grocery supply business, which supplies disposable products to supermarkets and other groceries, it has not been profitable, Chairman Ray Mundt said.

The sale is "in keeping with our mission of building value for shareholders over the long term," he said in a statement. "We expect to reinvest the proceeds in our successful supply systems businesses."
Berwyn, Pa.-based Unisource said the sale price is subject to changes based on valuations at the time of the deal's closing, expected by Sept. 30.

Unisource's U.S. grocery supply systems business, which it started in 1993, has more than $300 million in annual revenues. Unisource also operates a successful grocery supply distribution business in Canada which is integrated with its supply systems operations there.
Grocery supplies account for nearly a quarter of Unisource Canada's supply systems revenues, and Unisource is "fully committed to that business and intends to grow it aggressively," Mundt said.

Unisource, with annual revenues in excess of $7 billion, makes plastic films and containers, corrugated containers, packaging equipment and supplies. Bunzl, which had 1996 revenues of 1.8 billion pounds ($2.9 billion), makes paper and plastic products.
Unisource stock fell 37.5 cents to $19.375 in early afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
